scope: Read-only targeted source and saved baseline05 review, not a new simulation, mirror rollout, checkpoint inference or reward intervention. Installed files read with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES empty and standard library only.
conclusion: No definite joint-order, left/right default-pose, quaternion-order or velocity-frame implementation bug found in the reviewed path. Sideways drift remains an observed policy/physics outcome; this audit does not prove its unique cause or rule out unmeasured estimator/asset effects.

checks.detail: Native order is FL/FR/RL/RR hip, then FL/FR/RL/RR thigh, then FL/FR/RL/RR calf. JointPositionAction uses joint_names=[.*], preserve_order default false, all-joint slice; joint_pos_rel/joint_vel_rel also use all-joint native slice. Adapter does no joint permutation, scales/actions only clamp to100 before task action manager. Checkpoint660 was trained in this existing Lab convention, not a directly loaded original Go1 Gym actor. This is source/config consistency, not new physical joint-pulse validation.

Left hips+0.1, right hips-0.1; both front thighs0.8, both rear thighs1.0; all calves-1.5. Uniform action scale0.25 and configured PD25/0.5 apply to both sides. Front/rear stance difference is symmetric across left/right. This does not prove entire USD collision/inertia geometry has perfect mirror symmetry.

checks.item: XY reward and HIM velocity supervision frames
checks.detail: Actual installed track_lin_vel_xy_exp subtracts root_lin_vel_b[:2] from body command[:2], std0.5 gives original denominator0.25. Critic base_lin_vel reads the same root_lin_vel_b with observation scale2; HIM supervision45:48 therefore learns scaled body linear velocity. Estimated velocity is concatenated directly to actor, preserving original trained scale. Reward uses unscaled physical velocity as expected. Pinned PhysX root_com_lin_vel_b inverse-rotates world COM velocity using root_link_quat_w. No world/body or2x mismatch found.

Actual track_ang_vel_z_exp compares body yaw-rate command with root_ang_vel_b.z; actor angular velocity observes the same field scaled0.25. Evaluator reads xyzw quaternion, sends clamp(-yaw,+/-0.5) at gain1, disables parent heading/standing overwrite and updates current actor/critic command slots. Training uses stock heading stiffness0.5 and heading target0; this known gain difference is not an axis/sign inversion. Logged yaw command is based on pre-step yaw; small discrepancy from post-step trace yaw is expected.

checks.item: Baseline physical asymmetry from random COM
checks.detail: Standard stair evaluation removes startup add_base_mass/base_com/gain randomization unless eval_dynamics is enabled. Baseline05 base mass6.92100048065kg is constant; saved base COM y=0 for checked first rows. Material events remain caller supplied. Thus observed baseline drift cannot be attributed to the extra training COM randomization solely from domain_profile=none. Training domain none retains stock startup events; evaluation must use its flag/readbacks.

Four saved seed11/case15/env480 rows show both yaw and recomputed body lateral speed negative during descent; at6s yaw=-0.06344, worldvy=-0.07353, bodyvy=-0.05537, yawcmd=+0.06235. Recomputed bodyvy uses full Euler inverse rotation from saved yaw/roll/pitch, not a yaw-only approximation. Env480 succeeded; its trace is representative, not any of the25 failed individual episodes. Trace contains no estimated velocity or encoder latent, so this audit cannot measure estimator bias.

unimplemented_reward_options.rationale: Body lateral drift exists in representative traces, so changing yaw alone may not remove it.1.5 is also the stock Go2 tracking weight, but is not released Go1 paper weight.
unimplemented_reward_options.risks: Also increases forward-speed incentive; possible descent impacts, no direct world lateral-position constraint.

unimplemented_reward_options.rationale: Persistent negative yaw contributes world lateral drift alongside bodyvy.0.75 is stock Go2 weight, but not released Go1 paper weight.
unimplemented_reward_options.risks: More frequent/stronger turning correction can disturb gait; cannot by itself eliminate nonzero bodyvy.

evidence_limit: Compare each option independently to a common control and budget after the four planned arms. No claim that either change causes better smoothness/completion; no new external lateral controller is proposed.
